slides.text: Hallstatt, Austria. Squeezed between a lake and a mountain, the graveyard can't grow.
So 10 to 15 years after a burial, the grave was opened again to make room.
From around 1720, families bleached the skulls in the sun and painted them: flowers, crosses, names, dates.
About 1,200 skulls sit in the bone house. 610 are painted.
The newest arrived in 1995: a woman who asked, in her will, to be placed here.
